correctness.rationale: For each free edge direction j, squared distance equals the sum of squared near-face gaps in the other d-1 coordinates; minimizing j removes the largest gap, so T_d² is the sum of the d-1 smallest squared iid Uniform[0,1] gaps. Joint order-statistic density d! gives an exact ordered-ball integral weighted 1-u_(d-1). Below t=1, homogeneity gives polynomial a_d t^(d-1)-b_d t^d. For 1<t<sqrt2 the clipped region has one coordinate v>1 and the others in an orthant ball; integrating its negative weight gives the stated positive correction. Beta integration yields K_d ε^((d+2)/2), hence sharp one-sided differentiability order. d=3 polar/arcsin integration, shrinking simplex at center for ε^d upper tail, and E(sum U_i²-max U_i²) produce the remaining formulas. Independently tested d=3 CDF at 8 points against order-statistic quadrature, exact endpoint and mean for d=3,4,5,9. Numerical checks do not replace the all-dimensional argument.

value.rationale: The Euclidean distance from an interior random point to the cubical wireframe is a natural clearance statistic. Its exact threshold at half-side is canonical—the first reach of a tubular neighborhood to the opposite faces. The sharp cusp order/constant, complete cubic distribution and center-tail law give concrete geometry across arbitrary dimensions; these are not implied by the already-known low-radius intersection volume or by generic two-point distances. Full d>3 middle CDF is explicitly outside scope.

final_claim: For a volume-uniform point in a d-cube, d>=3, Euclidean clearance to its one-skeleton has exact low-radius polynomial and first-clipping integral with cusp exponent (d+2)/2 and positive coefficient, complete d=3 CDF, support endpoint sqrt(d-1), universal upper-tail constant, and exact second moment.
